newsitem.title: USA: Aon to cut 2,600 jobs in A&A integration.
newsitem.headline: Aon to cut 2,600 jobs in A&A integration.

text.p: Aon Corp., a major Chicago-based insurance broker, said it expects to lay off about 2,600 people over the next year as a result of its $1.23 billion acquisition of Alexander & Alexander Services Inc., the world's fourth largest insurance broker.

In a recent filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the insurance giant said about $40 million of the $145 million pretax special charges announced with 1997 first quarter earnings is attributed to the job terminations.

Aon has purchased three of its larger rivals in the last eight months. In October, it spent about $250 million to buy British broker Bain Hogg, the 11th largest insurance broker in the world. Last month, it agreed to buy London-based Minet Group from St. Paul Cos. Inc. for an undisclosed price.
In December, Aon agreed to buy A&A for $17.50 in cash per common share. The deal closed in January.
